alexcrichton commented on issue #10740:

Thanks for the report, and seems reasonable to fix! I got about halfway through removing/resolving the differences between LinearMemory and RuntimeLinearMemory but never finished the work, and I think that would probably help here. Agreed we should fix this though, and if you're interested to work on it I'd be happy to help review a PR.

V0ldek commented on issue #10740:

What would you see as a good fix here?

I'm not sure what the invariants for the code in vm/memory.rs are, but if it needs to know if the memory is mmapped or not then I was thinking maybe instead of LinearMemory::as_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 there should be LinearMemory::as_base(&self) -> MemoryBase that explicitly says if this is just any pointer or an mmap?

alexcrichton commented on issue #10740:

Unfortunately I don't think there's any fix for this right now without changing the APIs themselves. You're right though in that the fix will be somewhere around here. Personally I'd like to remove the need for LinearMemoryProxy and changing the raw runtime internals to "just" using LinearMemory, updating the signatures as necessary to morally match RuntimeLinearMemory. I'm not certain we'll want MemoryBase as an externally-facing abstraction, though.

I'd like to be able to access the specific Box<dyn LinearMemory> out of an Instance after it's instantiated. Currently it doesn't seem to be possible even in host functions that get a Caller.

alexcrichton commented on issue #10740:

The change here, what I think is your confusion, and part of my confusion, is I believe downstream of #9687. In that commit image management changed to hold an Arc<Mmap> internally within image slots which public external users of Wasmtime are unable to provide since that's an internal type. The PR says:

One option would be to sort-of-revert that change where MemoryImageSlot holds a raw pointer to the mmap that it's manipulating, and at that point I think it should be possible to delete RuntimeLinearMemory with some light refactoring, making LinearMemory the One True Abstraction, meaning that this issue should get resolved. I don't fully understand the consequences of such a change, however, because I'm not sure what the future work was lined up after #9687.

@sunshowers if you don't mind me pinging you on this, would you perhaps be able to shed some light on this? Specifically for you, your historical PR to Wasmtime, https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/pull/9687, hinted at future work which built on the refactorings you were working on, but I'm not sure what that future work was. I'm not sure if that would become reliant on memory-image-mapping holding strong references to Mmap internals of where the image is mapped into which would constraint the API and design of possible solution for this issue. If it was mostly just shuffling things around thats where, to solve this issue, it might make sense to undo some of the refactorings there but I don't want to be too hasty about that.

I'm not sure myself, but memory mappings are notoriously different across platforms, even Windows and Linux for example. I'm not an expert on memory mappings in general to know if there are any platforms which require specific knowledge of how the backing memory for a file mapping is memory-mapped.

V0ldek commented on issue #10740:

One important finding is that I think this is only an issue for the CoW mechanism. When setting memory_init_cow(false), the code works as is now. In particular, a workaround would be to always treat custom memories as Raw and bypass CoW, with the obvious downside of not allowing CoW.

Here's a small repro, it takes the memory_init_cow as a parameter and creates a simple custom mmap-backed memory. It panics when given true but works when given false:

Cargo.toml:

[package]
name = "wasmtime-repro-10740"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[dependencies]
wasmtime = "=49.0.3"
rustix = { version = "1", features = ["mm"] }

src/main.rs:

//! Usage: repro-10740-v49 <memory_init_cow: true|false>

use rustix::mm::{MapFlags, MprotectFlags, ProtFlags, mmap_anonymous, mprotect, munmap};
use std::ptr::null_mut;
use std::sync::Arc;
use wasmtime::*;

struct CustomMmapMemory {
    base: usize,
    mapped: usize,
    size: usize,
    capacity: usize,
}

impl CustomMmapMemory {
    /// Reserves `reserve + guard` bytes as `PROT_NONE` and makes `size` bytes read/write, growing in place up to `reserve`.
    fn new(minimum: usize, reserve: usize, guard: usize) -> Result<Self> {
        let mapped = reserve + guard;
        let base =
            unsafe { mmap_anonymous(null_mut(), mapped, ProtFlags::empty(), MapFlags::PRIVATE)? };
        if minimum > 0 {
            unsafe { mprotect(base, minimum, MprotectFlags::READ | MprotectFlags::WRITE)? };
        }
        Ok(Self {
            base: base as usize,
            mapped,
            size: minimum,
            capacity: reserve,
        })
    }
}

impl Drop for CustomMmapMemory {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe { munmap(self.base as *mut _, self.mapped).expect("munmap failed") };
    }
}

unsafe impl LinearMemory for CustomMmapMemory {
    fn byte_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }

    fn byte_capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.capacity
    }

    fn grow_to(&mut self, new_size: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if new_size > self.capacity {
            bail!("cannot grow beyond the reservation");
        }
        unsafe {
            mprotect(
                (self.base + self.size) as *mut _,
                new_size - self.size,
                MprotectFlags::READ | MprotectFlags::WRITE,
            )?;
        }
        self.size = new_size;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.base as *mut u8
    }
}

struct CustomMemoryCreator;

unsafe impl MemoryCreator for CustomMemoryCreator {
    fn new_memory(
        &self,
        _ty: MemoryType,
        minimum: usize,
        maximum: Option<usize>,
        reserved_size_in_bytes: Option<usize>,
        guard_size_in_bytes: usize,
    ) -> std::result::Result<Box<dyn LinearMemory>, String> {
        let reserve = reserved_size_in_bytes
            .or(maximum)
            .unwrap_or(1 << 30)
            .max(minimum);
        Ok(Box::new(
            CustomMmapMemory::new(minimum, reserve, guard_size_in_bytes)
                .map_err(|r| r.to_string())?,
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let cow: bool = match std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() {
        Some("true") => true,
        Some("false") => false,
        _ => {
            eprintln!("usage: wasmtime-repro-10740 <memory_init_cow: true|false>");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    let mut config = Config::new();
    config.with_host_memory(Arc::new(CustomMemoryCreator));
    config.memory_init_cow(cow);
    let engine = Engine::new(&config)?;

    // The active data segment is what produces a CoW memory image.
    let module = Module::new(
        &engine,
        r#"
        (module
          (memory (export "mem") 1)
          (data (i32.const 0) "hello")
          (func (export "load") (param i32) (result i32)
            (i32.load8_u (local.get 0))))
        "#,
    )?;

    let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
    println!("memory_init_cow = {cow}; instantiating...");
    let instance = Instance::new(&mut store, &module, &[])?;
    let load = instance.get_typed_func::<i32, i32>(&mut store, "load")?;
    let byte = load.call(&mut store, 1)?;
    println!(
        "load(1) = {byte:?} ({:?}), expected 'e'",
        byte as u8 as char
    );
    assert_eq!(byte, i32::from(b'e'));
    Ok(())
}

Here's a small repro, it takes the memory_init_cow as a parameter and creates a simple custom mmap-backed memory. It panics when given true but works when given false:

use rustix::mm::{MapFlags, MprotectFlags, ProtFlags, mmap_anonymous, mprotect, munmap};
use std::ptr::null_mut;
use std::sync::Arc;
use wasmtime::*;

struct CustomMmapMemory {
    base: usize,
    mapped: usize,
    size: usize,
    capacity: usize,
}

impl CustomMmapMemory {
    /// Reserves `reserve + guard` bytes as `PROT_NONE` and makes `size` bytes read/write, growing in place up to `reserve`.
    fn new(minimum: usize, reserve: usize, guard: usize) -> Result<Self> {
        let mapped = reserve + guard;
        let base =
            unsafe { mmap_anonymous(null_mut(), mapped, ProtFlags::empty(), MapFlags::PRIVATE)? };
        if minimum > 0 {
            unsafe { mprotect(base, minimum, MprotectFlags::READ | MprotectFlags::WRITE)? };
        }
        Ok(Self {
            base: base as usize,
            mapped,
            size: minimum,
            capacity: reserve,
        })
    }
}

impl Drop for CustomMmapMemory {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        unsafe { munmap(self.base as *mut _, self.mapped).expect("munmap failed") };
    }
}

unsafe impl LinearMemory for CustomMmapMemory {
    fn byte_size(&self) -> usize {
        self.size
    }

    fn byte_capacity(&self) -> usize {
        self.capacity
    }

    fn grow_to(&mut self, new_size: usize) -> Result<()> {
        if new_size > self.capacity {
            bail!("cannot grow beyond the reservation");
        }
        unsafe {
            mprotect(
                (self.base + self.size) as *mut _,
                new_size - self.size,
                MprotectFlags::READ | MprotectFlags::WRITE,
            )?;
        }
        self.size = new_size;
        Ok(())
    }

    fn as_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.base as *mut u8
    }
}

struct CustomMemoryCreator;

unsafe impl MemoryCreator for CustomMemoryCreator {
    fn new_memory(
        &self,
        _ty: MemoryType,
        minimum: usize,
        maximum: Option<usize>,
        reserved_size_in_bytes: Option<usize>,
        guard_size_in_bytes: usize,
    ) -> std::result::Result<Box<dyn LinearMemory>, String> {
        let reserve = reserved_size_in_bytes
            .or(maximum)
            .unwrap_or(1 << 30)
            .max(minimum);
        Ok(Box::new(
            CustomMmapMemory::new(minimum, reserve, guard_size_in_bytes)
                .map_err(|r| r.to_string())?,
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let cow: bool = match std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() {
        Some("true") => true,
        Some("false") => false,
        _ => {
            eprintln!("usage: wasmtime-repro-10740 <memory_init_cow: true|false>");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    let mut config = Config::new();
    config.with_host_memory(Arc::new(CustomMemoryCreator));
    config.memory_init_cow(cow);
    let engine = Engine::new(&config)?;

    // The active data segment is what produces a CoW memory image.
    let module = Module::new(
        &engine,
        r#"
        (module
          (memory (export "mem") 1)
          (data (i32.const 0) "hello")
          (func (export "load") (param i32) (result i32)
            (i32.load8_u (local.get 0))))
        "#,
    )?;

    let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
    println!("memory_init_cow = {cow}; instantiating...");
    let instance = Instance::new(&mut store, &module, &[])?;
    let load = instance.get_typed_func::<i32, i32>(&mut store, "load")?;
    let byte = load.call(&mut store, 1)?;
    println!(
        "load(1) = {byte:?} ({:?}), expected 'e'",
        byte as u8 as char
    );
    assert_eq!(byte, i32::from(b'e'));
    Ok(())
